clue.text: Cancel immediately, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the phrase for immediately is to be taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: immediately means right off, at once

explanation.surface: Someone demanding an order be revoked on the spot, as reported to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks a homophone: RIGHT OFF, meaning straight away, is said the same as the phrase meaning to cancel a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off a debt or loss is to cancel it as unrecoverable.

clue.text: Successfully breaking the law can result in it

definitions.text: Successfully breaking the law can result in it

indicators.note: breaking here means the words the law are smashed apart and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that crime, done well, pays handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' tells you to rearrange the letters of THE LAW; the whole clue is also the definition, since successful crime brings riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches are what a successful criminal hopes to gain, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: He succeeds in transmuting their gold

indicators.note: transmuting means changing one thing into another, so the letters of their are reworked

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An alchemist's apprentice making his name by turning their metal into gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' looks like triumph but means taking over from someone; 'transmuting' signals rearranging the letters of their.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir succeeds to property or a title when its holder dies, so he is the one who comes next.

clue.text: Building uninsured if I cease to provide cover for it

indicators.note: to provide cover for it says the words before wrap around the answer, concealing it within their letters

explanation.surface: An insurer warning that a property goes unprotected once they stop the policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The insurance story makes 'cover' look like a policy; here it means the words uninsured if I cease literally enclose the answer, running across their word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure, a grand word for a construction.

clue.text: Sell for double

definitions.meaning: goods that sell for a sum bring in that price
a ghostly double is the apparition of a living person

explanation.definitionFit: A painting may fetch a high price, meaning sell for it; a fetch is also the wraith or doppelganger of someone still alive.

clue.text: Gets worn in the first of several strikes

indicators.note: the first of picks out only the opening letter of the word several

parts.note: strikes as verb means cuffs, hits with an open hand

explanation.surface: A boxer bruised early on by the opening blows of a flurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets worn' suggests tiredness but means becomes scraped, as shoes do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that scuffs becomes marked and abraded through wear.

clue.text: Here's the main part of 22

parts.note: 22 is the unpowered aircraft of 22 down; the clue points to the space in its fuselage where the pilot sits, the part that matters most

explanation.definitionFit: The cockpit is the compartment of an aircraft from which it is flown, the chief part for its pilot.

clue.text: Give up oriental game to leading pro

indicators.note: to leading says the game is attached behind the word for pro, which comes first

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
go is the Japanese board game of black and white stones

explanation.surface: A professional quits after an Eastern board game proves too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the strategy game from East Asia; 'to leading' places the word for pro in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to do without it, to relinquish it voluntarily.

clue.text: Roughly speaking what greengrocers do with a cloth border?

indicators.note: roughly speaking signals an approximate spoken match, so the trade phrase is said loosely

parts.note: greengrocers sell veg, vegetables, for a living

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about how produce sellers use a fabric's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly speaking' gives a loose homophone: SELL VEG, what a greengrocer (a vegetable seller) does, said quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A selvedge is the woven edge of fabric that stops it fraying, its finished border.

clue.text: To avoid work eat abroad (about £1)

indicators.note: about means the French verb goes round the money that follows

parts.note: manger is French for to eat, eating as done abroad
L stands for pound, from Latin libra
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge the office by dining overseas for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' asks for a foreign word: MANGER, French for eat. 'about' puts L (pound) and I (one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to feign illness so as to shirk duty.

clue.text: Waits for production of this book

definitions.text: Waits for production of this book

parts.words: Waits for production of this book
parts.note: waits are carol singers who go round at Christmas; a Dickens story about a miser is named after their song

explanation.walkthrough: 'Waits' looks like a verb but is the old word for street carol singers; Dickens's famous ghost story is titled after a seasonal song.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's 1843 novella of Scrooge is named after the seasonal song that waits perform.

clue.text: Such edible delight

parts.note: the clue completes the name of a jelly sweet dusted with icing sugar, a delight from Istanbul

explanation.definitionFit: Lokum, the sugared jelly sweet, is known in English as the delight named after the country of Istanbul.

clue.text: I am quietly learning to beg

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
lore is learning, traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A shy student pleading under their breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead earnestly.

clue.text: Giving speech, don't start being inaudible

indicators.note: don't start tells the solver to drop the opening letter of the synonym

parts.note: muttering is speaking so low as to be barely heard

explanation.surface: Advice to a nervous speaker not to begin by mumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start' removes the M of MUTTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttering words is voicing them aloud.

clue.text: Cutting in is vice to be punished

indicators.note: to be punished suggests the words are beaten into a new shape, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A moral remark that pushing in is a wrong deserving penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be punished' rearranges the letters of IN IS VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisive remarks are sharp and penetrating, as a blade is.

clue.text: The long, not the Spanish, leather

indicators.note: not says the Spanish article is to be left out of the phrase before it

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A remark about a long leather strap of non-Spanish origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes EL, Spanish for 'the', from THE LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of hide used as a lace or whip.

clue.text: Stone might be so obsolete

definitions.meaning: the stone of a date fruit is removed when it is taken out of the fruit
no longer current or in use

explanation.definitionFit: A stone pulled from a date is out of the date; anything outdated is no longer current.

clue.text: Trample on a piece of cake

definitions.meaning: to tread all over someone, treat them with contempt

explanation.definitionFit: To walk over someone is to trample them; a walkover is an easy win.

clue.text: Island in which a river flowed

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
flowed means ran

explanation.surface: An island where a river once flowed.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAN is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is an island off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Offensive order given during a row

indicators.note: during says the order is placed within the row, inside it

parts.note: a row is a din, noise
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An insulting command barked during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' here (a din), not a line of seats; OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or disgusting.

clue.text: Conquistador's not finished holding surgeon in warship

indicators.note: holding means the shortened name contains the surgeon inside it
not finished cuts the final letter from the name

parts.note: Cortes was the Spanish conquistador who conquered the Aztecs
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A Spanish conqueror with a doctor aboard a fighting ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts CORTES to CORTE; Hernán Cortés conquered Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, fast naval escort vessel.

clue.text: Former spouse sat in the open

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed

explanation.surface: An ex-partner sitting outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means unprotected and open to view.

clue.text: It's powerless to fly

parts.note: reads as something unable to fly, but describes an aircraft without an engine that flies all the same

explanation.definitionFit: A sailplane flies on air currents with no engine, so it is unpowered.

clue.text: Pools of it around in aircraft

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the aircraft

parts.note: kites are flown in the air, so they stand for aircraft

indicators.note: around means the word it is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Swimming pools seen from planes overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns IT into TI. 'Pools' means pooled funds, not water.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a shared pot of money that players pool.

clue.text: Colour can turn up for instance

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: Paint pots revealed as examples of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour.

clue.text: Promising youngster sated with Ruritania?

parts.note: Ruritania is the imaginary kingdom invented by the novelist Anthony Hope
sated means full, written as the suffix -ful

explanation.surface: A young person stuffed full of an imaginary kingdom's romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony HOPE created Ruritania in The Prisoner of Zenda, so a head full of Ruritania is full of Hope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful is a candidate who aspires to success.

clue.text: Husky, they say, is a beast of burden

indicators.note: they say means the word for husky is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a husky voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: A sled dog described as a pack animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' suggests the sled dog, but it is the adjective meaning rough-voiced: HOARSE, said like HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses have long carried loads, the classic pack animal.

clue.text: Uninvolved as car crashes in the vicinity of Victoria

indicators.note: crashes means the words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bystander's car crashes near Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashes' rearranges UNINVOLVED AS CAR. Victoria, capital of British Columbia, lies on the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria, British Columbia's capital, stands at the island's southern tip.

clue.text: Did a dance having brought in the catch

definitions.meaning: danced a reel, a lively Scottish dance
wound in a fish on a fishing line

explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to dance a reel; an angler reeled in a catch.

clue.text: Bowler, for instance, had to agree to differ

indicators.note: to differ signals the letters change from their written order

explanation.surface: A bowler who had to accept disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' is the hat, not the cricketer; 'to differ' rearranges HAD AGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is one example of something worn on the head.
